name: Yasuní National Park
blurb: Fruit trees, peccaries and monkeys, and the jaguars and harpy eagles above them.

tip.title: Remove the jaguars
tip.text: Jaguars hunt peccaries, tapirs and agoutis. Set Jaguar to -100% and watch those plant-eaters, then the fruit trees they feed on.

notes: The species list comes from GBIF occurrence records inside a circle around the park, so it can include nearby areas. Feeding links come from GloBI records and the sources listed where they state them; others are general ecology and are illustrative.

nodes.name: Sunlight
nodes.desc: Light that filters down through the tall canopy to the plants that drive the forest's food web.

nodes.name: Rainfall
nodes.desc: Constant moisture in this wet Amazon forest keeps its trees growing and fruiting.

nodes.name: Forest soil
nodes.desc: Soil and leaf litter hold the nutrients that trees take up again after decomposers release them.

nodes.name: Fungi & bacteria
nodes.desc: Break down fallen leaves, fruit and dead animals, returning nutrients to the forest floor.

nodes.name: Wild cacao relative
nodes.desc: A forest tree whose fruit is eaten by peccaries, deer, agoutis and monkeys, according to GloBI feeding records.

nodes.name: Guarea tree
nodes.desc: A rainforest tree whose fruit is recorded in GloBI as food for tapirs and toucans.

nodes.name: Dendropanax tree
nodes.desc: A forest tree whose fruit is recorded in GloBI as food for monkeys, toucans and other birds.

nodes.name: Leonia tree
nodes.desc: A rainforest tree whose fruit is recorded in GloBI as food for monkeys and many fruit-eating birds.

nodes.name: Lowland tapir
nodes.desc: Browses leaves, shoots and fruit and is described as an important seed disperser. Jaguars, caimans and anacondas prey on it.

nodes.name: White-lipped peccary
nodes.desc: Herd animal that eats mostly fruit and other plant parts. Wikipedia calls it important prey for large cats.

nodes.name: Collared peccary
nodes.desc: Eats fruit and other plant material and is a common jaguar prey animal in Amazonian forests.

nodes.name: Red brocket
nodes.desc: A forest deer that eats fruit and leaves. Recorded in GloBI eating Theobroma fruit and as jaguar prey.

nodes.name: Black agouti
nodes.desc: A forest rodent that eats fruit and seeds. It is prey for jaguars, ocelots and harpy eagles.

nodes.name: Brown woolly monkey
nodes.desc: A canopy primate that eats fruit. Monkeys of this kind are among harpy eagle prey.

nodes.name: White-throated toucan
nodes.desc: The most recorded bird near Yasuni. Large-billed fruit eater that swallows fruit whole.

nodes.name: Gaudy grasshopper
nodes.desc: A leaf-eating grasshopper of the forest understorey, food for lizards and other insect-eaters.

nodes.name: Brown-eared anole
nodes.desc: A small forest lizard that eats insects. The blunthead treesnake is recorded in GloBI eating it.

nodes.name: Blunthead treesnake
nodes.desc: A slender tree snake recorded in GloBI eating anoles.

nodes.name: Ocelot
nodes.desc: A medium-sized forest cat that hunts small mammals such as agoutis, and lizards.

nodes.name: Jaguar
nodes.desc: The top predator. GloBI records it eating peccaries, brocket deer, tapirs, agoutis and pacas, and it also takes caiman in floodplains.

nodes.name: Harpy eagle
nodes.desc: Canopy raptor that eats mostly sloths and monkeys, plus agoutis, snakes and birds.
